sentence.english: Money is overrated. Truly new things rarely need an abundance of money. If that was so, billionaires would have a monopoly on inventing new things, and they don’t. Instead, almost all breakthroughs are made by those who lack money. If breakthroughs could be bought, then the rich would buy them. Instead, passion, persistence, belief, and ingenuity are required to invent new things—qualities the poor and young often have in abundance. Stay hungry.
sentence.persian: به پول بیشتر از حد بها می‌دن. چیزهای واقعاً تازه به‌ندرت به پول فراوون نیاز دارن. وگرنه اختراع چیزهای تازه در انحصار میلیاردرها بود، که نیست. تقریباً همه‌ی جهش‌های بزرگ کار کساییه که پول کافی ندارن. اگه می‌شد این جهش‌ها رو خرید، ثروتمندها می‌خریدنشون. برای اختراع، شور و اشتیاق، پشتکار، باور و ابتکار لازمه؛ چیزهایی که آدم‌های کم‌پول و جوون اغلب فراوون دارن. تشنه‌ی پیشرفت بمون.

meaning: A useful novel result requires passionate, persistent, ingenious experimentation; funds can supply materials but cannot substitute for discovery.

a.summaryFa: یک ظرف تقریباً خالی از سکه مانع ساختن آب‌رسانی ساده برای گیاهان نمی‌شود؛ آزمون و اصلاح، فکر را به وسیله‌ای کارآمد تبدیل می‌کند.
a.storyFa: آدمک سبز پول خرید دستگاه آمادهٔ آبیاری را ندارد. به‌جای منتظرماندن، با بطری و لولهٔ ساده نمونه می‌سازد؛ آبِ نمونهٔ اول بیش از حد سریع خارج می‌شود. با مشاهده و اصلاح، گیره‌ای برای تنظیم جریان می‌گذارد و سرانجام قطره‌های آرام گیاه را آبیاری می‌کنند. کمبود پول از راه ابتکار و پیگیری حل می‌شود.
a.meaningFa: پول فراوان جانشین فکر و پیگیری نیست؛ راه‌حل تازه از علاقه به یک مسئله، امتحان‌کردن و بهترکردن طرح به دست می‌آید.
a.scene:
Composition: THREE broad horizontal watercolor story strips, top then middle then bottom, square overall. Keep each strip exceptionally simple with one GREEN adult figure fully inside it, all feet visible. Clear difference between a ready-made expensive product and a useful modest homemade invention.
TOP: in a small garden-supply shop, GREEN looks at an elegant automatic plant-watering kit on a low display stand: a compact water tank, pump and hose next to a potted plant. One price tag with just a conspicuous cluster of many little coin symbols, NO text. GREEN opens a small purse in its hand with only THREE coins visible, clearly less than the tag suggests. Its face is thoughtful rather than ashamed. GREEN's bubble reads exactly: «پولم به این نمی‌رسه.» A gentle vendor need not appear. No other shop products or clutter.
MIDDLE: at GREEN's modest home balcony, GREEN has begun its OWN solution with a transparent used water bottle held upright on a little wooden stand above one potted plant. One transparent tube runs from the bottom of the bottle down into the plant soil. This first attempt lets water pour too fast, visibly making a little puddle in the pot saucer. GREEN watches that specific flaw closely and thoughtfully, reaching toward a plain wooden clothespin on the low workbench. Its bubble reads exactly: «یه بار دیگه!» A small rejected bottle prototype lies beside the bench, not in the walking path. All hands must connect naturally to two arms.
BOTTOM: same home plant, GREEN, bottle and stand. The meaningful improvement is a simple wooden clothespin now clamping the tube almost closed. Only a few separated slow drops leave the tube into the soil, dry pot saucer. Keep the whole bottle-tube-clip-plant system large and crystal clear. GREEN smiles with quiet pride and adjusts the clothespin, looking at the controlled drops. The two unsuccessful bottle prototypes remain neatly near the same modest bench and the little purse remains nearly empty. No success comes from money or magic. The useful solution is an ingenious design change discovered through persistence. No further text. Moderate watercolor and balanced adult shapes; no tiny diagram labels.

b.summaryFa: یک نوازنده با هر دو دست ساز می‌زند؛ دوستش با قطعات ساده و چند بار آزمون، راهی برای ورق‌زدن نت با پدال پیدا می‌کند.
b.storyFa: آدمک بنفش هنگام نواختن پیانو برای ورق‌زدن نت ناچار است نواختن را قطع کند. آدمک صورتی با سکه‌های اندکش سراغ ساختن ورق‌زن پدالی می‌رود؛ یک نمونهٔ خمیده و یک صفحهٔ مچاله نشان می‌دهند راه‌حل از اول آماده نبوده است. در قاب آخر نوازنده با هر دو دست می‌نوازد و پایش پدال متصل به بازوی کوچک ورق‌زن را فشار می‌دهد.
b.meaningFa: یک نیاز واقعی، اشتیاق به کمک و تکرار آزمایش‌ها به اختراع می‌رسد؛ انبوه پول به‌تنهایی این مرحلهٔ کشف و ساختن را انجام نمی‌دهد.
b.scene:
Composition: TWO broad horizontal panels, top then bottom. A very simple upright piano on the right of each scene, keyboard and sheet-music rest both visible, a PURPLE adult musician and a PINK adult inventor with only two fine lashes, otherwise identical neutral body. Both entire bodies and feet remain visible; use a modest adult scale that fits both wide panels. The innovation is a mechanical foot-operated page-turner made from a simple pedal, a cord and one hinged wooden arm with a small soft clip.
TOP: PURPLE is sitting on a piano stool; one hand has just left the keyboard to awkwardly reach to turn a page, while the other rests on keys. PURPLE's interrupted playing and wish are clear. Its bubble says exactly: «کاش بدون دست ورق می‌خورد!» PINK stands beside a small low workbench, looking with interested empathy at this precise problem and assembling a little wooden lever. On PINK's bench sit only THREE coins, a short cord, one wooden pedal and one discarded bent arm. A crumpled sheet lies next to the rejected prototype: evidence of experimentation rather than a pile of clutter. PINK has exactly two arms, each attached naturally, no third hands.
BOTTOM: same piano, same musician and inventor. The working page-turner is now clearly mounted at the side of the music rest: one slender hinged wooden arm with a soft clip catches the free edge of exactly one page and is visibly lifting that one page into a curved turning arc. The page remains partly attached at the sheet music fold. A visible simple cord runs from this hinged arm down the outside of the piano to a single wooden foot pedal on the floor beside PURPLE's foot. PURPLE's foot presses that dedicated pedal; BOTH hands stay naturally on the keyboard, happily playing. This is NOT one of the built-in piano pedals. PINK, standing to the side with relaxed arms and a pleased modest smile, watches the result. PINK's bubble says exactly: «بالاخره شد!» Rejected wooden arms remain on the low bench, and three coins remain visible. Keep the curved page, hinged arm, cord and dedicated foot pedal very simple and legible; no magical floating sheet, no extra hands or complicated machine. No music notation text, only sparse dark musical symbols if necessary. No other words.

c.summaryFa: برای چیدن میوهٔ دور از دست، پول خرید ابزار بزرگ ندارد؛ با آزمونِ چند سرِ متفاوت، میوه‌چینی می‌سازد که میوه را سالم می‌گیرد.
c.storyFa: آدمک بنفش زیر یک شاخهٔ دور از دست ایستاده است. نمونهٔ اولِ چنگکی، میوه را از شاخه جدا می‌کند اما نمی‌گیرد و روی پارچه می‌اندازد. آدمک تسلیم نمی‌شود و زیر حلقهٔ انتهای دسته، کیسهٔ نرم می‌گذارد. در پایان میوهٔ جداشده سالم داخل همین کیسه می‌افتد؛ چند طرح قبلی کنار سکه‌های کم مانده‌اند.
c.meaningFa: سازندگی از دیدن دقیقِ مشکل، باور به امکان حل‌کردن آن و اصلاح پیوسته می‌آید؛ هزینهٔ کم به‌خودی‌خود معجزه نمی‌کند و پول زیاد هم جای ابتکار را نمی‌گیرد.
c.scene:
Composition: THREE clear horizontal watercolor story strips, top then middle then bottom, square overall. The same single low garden tree on the left side of each strip, only its lower trunk and one fruit-bearing reachable-with-pole branch, and one PURPLE adult inventor on the right. Keep the whole adult and all feet inside each strip. Only two or three red apples on the branch; do not draw a huge orchard or dangerous heights. The low-cost invention is a long wooden fruit-picking pole with a simple round hoop and, finally, a soft cloth catching bag below the hoop. All mechanics must be easy to see.
TOP: PURPLE looks eagerly at one ripe red apple just beyond arm reach, next to a tiny workbench with a plain wooden pole, a metal wire hoop, a scrap of cloth and a small tin containing THREE coins. Its bubble says exactly: «با همین‌ها شروع می‌کنم.» A curious practical expression, no desperation. The idea is not 'being poor is virtuous'; the visible materials are enough to begin experimenting.
MIDDLE: PURPLE tests the first pole prototype, which has a small fork at its tip but no catching bag. The fork has just dislodged one red apple; it is falling past the bare fork onto a neatly spread soft folded cloth on the ground, so there is no injury. A short motion arc shows the uncontrolled fall. PURPLE reacts thoughtfully, not gleefully, notices that detaching is not enough. Its short bubble says exactly: «باید سالم هم بگیرتش!» Keep apple, fork, cloth and gaze consistent. No fruit magically grows back or duplicate same apple.
BOTTOM: PURPLE has ingeniously replaced the fork with a wide simple hoop and a clearly visible small soft cloth bag hanging below it, securing both to the end of the SAME pole. A ripe apple from the branch is now visibly captured inside the hanging cloth bag directly under the branch, not falling outside it. PURPLE supports the pole with both hands, quietly delighted. The earlier fork prototype and an unused larger awkward hoop rest neatly on the little workbench with the same coin tin, showing persistence and revisions. The final pole is neither expensive nor magical; the actual difference is the catching bag. No additional text. Use readable larger silhouettes, not tiny diagrams.

d.titleFa: ابزار را می‌خریم؛ فکر را می‌سازیم
d.summaryFa: خرید ابزار، راه‌حل آماده تحویل نمی‌دهد؛ دو همکار با آزمون و اصلاح نمونه، بالابر کوچکی برای کتاب‌ها می‌سازند.
d.storyFa: دو همکار فیروزه‌ای و نارنجی ابزارهای نو دارند، اما هنوز طرح مؤثری برای جابه‌جایی کتاب‌ها روی دو پله پیدا نکرده‌اند. آن‌ها از انباشت ابزار به کار مشترک روی یک نمونهٔ ساده می‌رسند. چند نمونهٔ کج و ناموفق کنار میز مانده است و بالابرِ اصلاح‌شده با دو ریل، کتاب‌ها را صاف بالا می‌برد.
d.meaningFa: پول می‌تواند ابزار بخرد، اما فکر نو، آزمون، پشتکار و همکاری را آماده تحویل نمی‌دهد؛ جهش با ساختن و اصلاح‌کردن شکل می‌گیرد.
d.scene:
Composition: TWO wide horizontal watercolor panels, top then bottom, square overall. Two adult collaborators: TEAL inventor and warm ORANGE inventor, same balanced neutral body shapes and no special clothes. A tiny neighborhood library workspace with TWO low interior steps leading to a low landing. They want to move stacks of books up those two steps easily. The invented device lifts BOOKS ONLY, never people. Keep all people, feet, two steps and complete simple mechanism inside the panels.
TOP: the two collaborators stand at a modest workbench. A few newly bought tools and two open new toolboxes sit on or beside it, with removed simple ribbon packaging. A large sheet of blank paper lies on the bench toward its readers, with only one small incomplete sketch of a box and pulley, no words. TEAL thoughtfully looks from the many available tools to the still-unsolved practical problem: three books wait at the foot of the two low steps. ORANGE is scratching its chin thoughtfully, not stupid or mocked. Their expression says tools alone have not supplied the solution. TEAL's bubble reads exactly: «ابزار داریم؛ راهش رو باید پیدا کنیم.» No caricature of wealth, no money thrown away, no giant luxury lab.
BOTTOM: after persistent collaborative experimentation, TEAL and ORANGE use a simple working hand-cranked book lift beside the same two steps. A small flat wooden platform sits level between TWO straight wooden guide rails. It holds three closed books at the low landing height. One rope attaches to the platform, passes over a single small pulley mounted on the top of the frame and runs down to TEAL's clearly visible hand crank. TEAL turns the crank naturally with one hand and steadies the frame with the other. ORANGE at the low landing comfortably receives one of the books, pleased. A tiny earlier crooked platform and two rejected little wooden supports sit neatly beside the workbench: evidence of tested failed prototypes. Avoid several ropes or gears; one mechanically readable frame, rails, platform, rope, pulley and crank. The actual creative improvement is adding two guides to stop the platform tipping. ORANGE's short bubble reads exactly: «فکر نو رو باید ساخت!» The available tools are useful but the discovery arose from work. Warm modest satisfaction, no triumphant trophy, no mystical money power. No other text, blank book covers, no labels or arrows.
